summary: If someone uses a house or other property for three full years, we assume it is his, like a chazakah. The Rabbis argue about a field that only gives crops part of the year, and how long its chazakah takes.

chunks.en: The chazakah of houses,
chunks.st: With regard to the presumptive ownership of houses;

words.note: Using property in a way that shows it belongs to you.

chunks.en: pits, ditches and caves,
chunks.st: and of pits; and of ditches; and of caves, which are used to collect water;

chunks.en: dovecotes and bathhouses,
chunks.st: and of dovecotes; and of bathhouses;

chunks.en: olive presses and watered fields,
chunks.st: and of olive presses; and of irrigated fields, which must be watered by people;

chunks.he: וְהָעֲבָדִים וְכָל שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה פֵרוֹת תָּדִיר,
chunks.en: and servants, and anything that gives fruit all the time:
chunks.st: and of slaves; and all similar property that constantly, i.e., throughout the year, generates profits,

chunks.en: their chazakah is three years, day after day.
chunks.st: their presumptive ownership is established by working and profiting from them for a duration of three years from day to day.
chunks.stMore: If the one in possession of the property can prove that he worked and profited from it for the previous three full years, there is a presumption that it belongs to him, and would remain in his possession if another were to claim that the property belonged to him or to his ancestors.

chunks.en: A field watered by rain:
chunks.st: With regard to a non-irrigated field,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one that is watered by rain, in which produce grows during certain seasons during the year,

words.note: A field that only gets water from the rain.

chunks.en: its chazakah is three years,
chunks.st: its presumption of ownership is established in three years,

chunks.en: but not day after day.
chunks.st: but they are not from day to day,
chunks.stMore: since the fields are not worked and harvested continually throughout the three-year period.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Three months in the first year, three in the last year,
chunks.st: Three months of possession in the first year, three months of possession in the last year,

chunks.en: and twelve months in the middle,
chunks.st: and twelve months of possession in the middle,

chunks.en: that makes eighteen months.
chunks.st: which are eighteen months,
chunks.stMore: suffice to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to a non-irrigated field.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: A month in the first year and a month in the last year,
chunks.st: A month of possession in the first year, and a month of possession in the last year,

chunks.en: and twelve months in the middle,
chunks.st: and twelve months of possession in the middle,

chunks.en: that makes fourteen months.
chunks.st: which are fourteen months,
chunks.stMore: suffice to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to a non-irrigated field.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael said:

chunks.en: When is this said?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement, that eighteen months are required for a non-irrigated field, said?

chunks.en: With a grain field.
chunks.st: It is said with regard to a white field [bisdeh lavan], i.e., a grain field.

words.note: A field of grain, with no trees.

chunks.en: But with a field of trees,
chunks.st: But with regard to a field of trees,

chunks.en: if he gathered his grain,
chunks.st: once he gathered his produce, and then

chunks.en: picked his olives,
chunks.st: harvested his olives, and then

chunks.en: and gathered his figs,
chunks.st: gathered his figs,

chunks.en: these count as three years.
chunks.st: these three harvests are the equivalent of three years.
chunks.stMore: Since he harvested three types of produce, this is equivalent to having possessed the field for three years.

summary: For a chazakah, Eretz Yisrael is split into three lands: Yehudah, the other side of the Yarden, and the Galil. The owner and the one using the land must be in the same land, so the owner can hear about it and come to protest.

chunks.en: There are three lands for chazakah:
chunks.st: There are three independent lands in Eretz Yisrael with regard to establishing presumptive ownership:

chunks.en: Yehudah, the other side of the Yarden, and the Galil.
chunks.st: Judea, and Transjordan, and the Galilee.

chunks.en: If the owner was in Yehudah and someone used his land in the Galil,
chunks.st: If the prior owner of the field was in Judea and another took possession of his field in the Galilee,

chunks.en: or he was in the Galil and someone used it in Yehudah,
chunks.st: or if he was in the Galilee and another took possession of his field in Judea,

chunks.en: it is not a chazakah,
chunks.st: the possessor does not establish presumptive ownership

chunks.en: unless the owner is with him in the same land.
chunks.st: until the one possessing the field will be with the prior owner in one province.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: They only said three years
chunks.st: The Sages said that establishing presumptive ownership requires three years

chunks.en: so that if the owner is in Spain, far away,
chunks.st: only in order that if the owner will be in Spain [Aspamya],

chunks.en: and someone uses his land for a year,
chunks.st: and another possesses his field for a year,

chunks.en: people go and tell him during a year,
chunks.st: people will go and inform the owner by the end of the next year,

chunks.en: and he comes back in the next year.
chunks.st: and the owner will come back in the following year and take the possessor to court.

summary: Using someone's land only counts as a chazakah if the person also has a reason why it is his, like that he bought it or got it as a gift. People who use property as part of their work or family, like a craftsman or a husband, cannot make a chazakah this way.

chunks.en: Any chazakah that does not come with a claim
chunks.st: Any possession that is not accompanied by a claim explaining how the possessor became the owner

chunks.en: is not a chazakah.
chunks.st: is not sufficient to establish the presumption of ownership.

chunks.en: How is that? If the owner said to him,
chunks.st: How so? If the prior owner said to the possessor:

chunks.en: What are you doing on my land?
chunks.explain: The person using the land has to give a reason why it is his.
chunks.st: What are you doing in my land?

chunks.en: And he answered him,
chunks.st: And the possessor said to him in response: I am in possession of the land

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר לִי אָדָם דָּבָר מֵעוֹלָם,
chunks.en: Because nobody ever said anything to me,
chunks.st: because no person ever said anything to me
chunks.stMore: about my being here, i.e., he states no valid claim as to why he would be the owner of the land,

chunks.en: this is not a chazakah.
chunks.st: his mere use is not sufficient to establish the presumption
chunks.stMore: of ownership. But if the possessor claimed: I am in possession of the land

chunks.en: But if he says: Because you sold it to me,
chunks.st: because you sold it to me,

chunks.en: because you gave it to me as a gift,
chunks.st: or: Because you gave it to me as a gift,

chunks.en: your father sold it to me,
chunks.st: or: Because your father sold it to me,

chunks.en: your father gave it to me as a gift,
chunks.st: or: Because your father gave it to me as a gift,
chunks.stMore: these are valid claims to ownership. In these cases, his possession

chunks.en: this is a chazakah.
chunks.st: is sufficient to establish the presumption of ownership.

chunks.en: And one who says he got it as a yerushah
chunks.st: And one who comes to claim the land based on inheritance

words.note: What children get from a parent who passed away.

chunks.en: does not need to give a reason.
chunks.st: does not need a claim
chunks.stMore: explaining why his ancestors had a right to the land.

chunks.en: Workers, partners, sharecroppers and guardians
chunks.st: Craftsmen who are in possession of items that they are repairing, and partners, and sharecroppers, and stewards [veha’apotropin]

words.note: Farmers who work someone else's field for part of the crop.

chunks.en: do not get a chazakah.
chunks.st: do not have the ability to establish the presumption
chunks.stMore: of ownership with regard to property in their possession, as their possession is not indicative of ownership.

chunks.en: A man does not get a chazakah in his wife's property,
chunks.st: Similarly, a man does not have the ability to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to his wife’s property,

chunks.en: and a woman not in her husband's property,
chunks.st: and a wife does not have the ability to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to her husband’s property.

chunks.en: and a father not in his son's property,
chunks.st: And a father similarly does not have the ability to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to a son’s property,

chunks.en: and a son not in his father's property.
chunks.explain: They use each other's things freely, so using it proves nothing.
chunks.st: and a son does not have the ability to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to a father’s property.
chunks.stMore: A husband and wife, or son and father, use each other’s property freely. Possession is therefore not indicative of ownership.

chunks.en: When is this said?
chunks.st: The mishna continues: In what case is this statement, that one establishes the presumption of ownership after profiting from the property for a certain duration, with the exception of the above people, said?

chunks.en: When someone just uses the land. But when someone gives a gift,
chunks.st: It is said in a case of one who has mere possession of the property, which does, in some cases, serve as proof of ownership. But in a case where another person gives one a gift,

chunks.en: or brothers who split up what they got,
chunks.st: or there are brothers who divided their inheritance,

chunks.en: or one who takes the property of a ger who died with no family,
chunks.st: or there is one who takes possession of the property of a convert
chunks.stMore: who died without heirs and his property is now ownerless,

chunks.en: if he locked a door, made a fence or broke a fence even a little,
chunks.st: as soon as one locked the door of the property, or fenced it or breached its fence even a bit,

chunks.en: this is a chazakah.
chunks.explain: Here this act makes the property his right away.
chunks.st: this is considered taking possession of the property, and it effects acquisition.

summary: If witnesses said someone used a field for three years, and they were proven to be lying witnesses, they must pay the owner the whole field. If different pairs testified about each year, they split the payment.

chunks.en: If two people testified about him
chunks.st: If there were two witnesses testifying on his behalf

chunks.en: that he ate from the field three years,
chunks.st: that he, the possessor of the land, worked and profited from a field for three years, and therefore has presumptive ownership,

chunks.en: and they were found to be lying witnesses,
chunks.st: and they were found to be conspiring
chunks.stMore: witnesses, as it was proven that they were not present to witness the matter about which they had testified,

words.note: Witnesses proven to have been somewhere else at the time.

chunks.en: they pay him everything.
chunks.st: they must pay the true owner of the field the full
chunks.stMore: value of the field that they attempted, through their testimony, to remove from his possession, as it is written in the Torah: “Then shall you do to him, as he had planned to do to his brother” (Deuteronomy 19:19).

chunks.en: If two testified about the first year,
chunks.st: If two witnesses testify that he worked and profited from the field during the first year,

chunks.en: and two about the second,
chunks.st: another two testify that he worked and profited from it during the second year,

chunks.en: and two about the third,
chunks.st: and another two testify that he worked and profited from it during the third,
chunks.stMore: and all were found to be conspiring witnesses, payment of the value of the field to the owner is

chunks.en: they split the payment three ways.
chunks.st: divided among them.

chunks.en: If three brothers testified, and one other person joined each of them,
chunks.st: If the testimony was given by three brothers, each of whom testify about one year, and another unrelated individual joined with each of the brothers as the second witness,

chunks.en: these are three separate testimonies,
chunks.st: these are three distinct testimonies
chunks.stMore: and they are accepted by the court. If they were to be considered one testimony, it would not be accepted, as brothers may not testify together.

chunks.en: but they are one testimony for being lying witnesses.
chunks.st: But they are one testimony for the purpose of rendering them as conspiring
chunks.stMore: witnesses, and the payment is divided among them.

summary: Some uses of a shared courtyard show ownership and some do not. Keeping an animal or an oven there is not a chazakah, but building a wall or a special place for them is.

chunks.en: These are things that make a chazakah,
chunks.st: These are uses of property that have the means to establish the presumption of ownership,

chunks.en: and these are things that do not make a chazakah.
chunks.st: and these are uses of property that do not have the means to establish the presumption of ownership:

chunks.en: If he kept an animal in the courtyard,
chunks.st: If one would stand an animal in a courtyard;

chunks.en: an oven or a stove,
chunks.st: or if one would place an oven, a millstone, or a stove there;

chunks.en: or a mill, or raised chickens,
chunks.st: or if one raises chickens in a courtyard,

chunks.en: or put his manure in the courtyard,
chunks.st: or places his fertilizer in a courtyard,

chunks.en: it is not a chazakah.
chunks.st: these actions are not sufficient to establish the presumption of ownership.

chunks.he: אֲבָל עָשָׂה מְחִצָּה לִבְהֶמְתּוֹ גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: But if he made a wall for his animal ten tefachim high,
chunks.st: But if one constructed a partition ten handbreadths high to contain his animal,

chunks.en: and the same for the oven,
chunks.st: and similarly if he constructed a partition for his oven,

chunks.en: and the same for the stove,
chunks.st: and similarly if he constructed a partition for his stove,

chunks.en: and the same for the mill,
chunks.st: and similarly if he constructed a partition for his millstone;

chunks.en: or he brought chickens into the house,
chunks.st: or if one brought chickens into the house,

chunks.en: or he made a place for his manure
chunks.st: or if he fashioned a place in the ground for his fertilizer that is

chunks.en: three tefachim deep or three tefachim high,
chunks.st: three handbreadths deep or three handbreadths high,

chunks.en: this is a chazakah.
chunks.st: these actions are sufficient to establish the presumption of ownership.

summary: This mishnah teaches which things sticking out of a house, like spouts, ladders, windows and beams, can become a chazakah. Small things that can easily be moved do not, but bigger, fixed ones do.

chunks.en: A spout does not have a chazakah,
chunks.st: With regard to a spout protruding from one’s roof gutter draining water into another’s property, its owner has no means to establish an acquired privilege for its use,

words.note: A short pipe at the end of a roof gutter.

chunks.en: but its place has a chazakah.
chunks.st: but he does have the means to establish an acquired privilege with regard to its place, as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: A long roof gutter has a chazakah.
chunks.st: With regard to a gutter pipe that traverses the length of the roof, one does have the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

chunks.en: An Egyptian ladder has no chazakah,
chunks.st: With regard to an Egyptian ladder, which is small and portable, one has no means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

words.note: A small ladder that can be moved.

chunks.en: but a Tyrian ladder has a chazakah.
chunks.st: But with regard to a Tyrian ladder, which is large and fixed in place, one does have the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

words.note: A big ladder fixed in place.

chunks.en: An Egyptian window has no chazakah,
chunks.st: With regard to an Egyptian window, one has no means to establish an acquired privilege for its use;

chunks.en: but a Tyrian window has a chazakah.
chunks.st: but with regard to a Tyrian window, one does have the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

chunks.en: What is an Egyptian window?
chunks.st: What is the defining feature of an Egyptian window?

chunks.en: Any window that a person's head
chunks.st: It is any window that is so small that a person’s head

chunks.en: cannot fit into.
chunks.st: is not able to fit inside it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If it has a frame,
chunks.st: If a window has a frame,

chunks.en: even though the head
chunks.st: even though a person’s head

chunks.en: of a person cannot fit into it,
chunks.st: is not able to fit inside it,

chunks.en: this is a chazakah.
chunks.st: one does have the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use.

chunks.en: A beam sticking out a tefach or more
chunks.st: With regard to a projection
chunks.stMore: emerging from the wall of one’s house, overhanging a courtyard,

words.note: A piece of wood sticking out from the wall.

chunks.en: has a chazakah,
chunks.st: one has the means to establish an acquired privilege for its use if it protrudes at least as far as a handbreadth,

chunks.en: and the neighbor can protest.
chunks.st: and the owner of the courtyard can protest its construction.

chunks.en: Less than a tefach:
chunks.st: If it protrudes less than a handbreadth,

chunks.en: it has no chazakah,
chunks.st: the owner of the house has no means to establish an acquired privilege for its use,

chunks.en: and the neighbor cannot protest.
chunks.st: and the owner of the courtyard cannot protest its construction.

summary: A person may not open new windows or doors into a courtyard he shares with others, because they need their privacy. Facing a public street, though, he may open as many doors and windows as he wants.

chunks.he: לֹא יִפְתַּח אָדָם חַלּוֹנוֹתָיו לַחֲצַר הַשֻּׁתָּפִין.
chunks.en: A person may not open his windows into a shared courtyard.
chunks.st: A person may not open his windows, i.e., build an opening in a wall to use as a window, into a courtyard belonging to partners, i.e., a courtyard in which he is a partner.

chunks.en: If he bought a house in another courtyard,
chunks.st: If he purchased a house in another, adjacent courtyard,

chunks.en: he may not open it into the shared courtyard.
chunks.st: he may not open the house into a courtyard belonging to partners.

chunks.en: If he built an upstairs room on top of his house,
chunks.st: If he built a loft on top of his house,

chunks.en: he may not open it into the shared courtyard.
chunks.st: he may not open it into a courtyard belonging to partners.

chunks.en: But if he wants,
chunks.st: Rather, if he desired to build a loft, he may

chunks.en: he builds a room inside his house,
chunks.st: build a room within his house,

chunks.en: or builds an upstairs room on top of his house
chunks.st: or he may build a loft on top of his house,

chunks.en: and opens it into his house.
chunks.st: and open it into his house, not directly into the courtyard.

chunks.he: לֹא יִפְתַּח אָדָם לַחֲצַר הַשֻּׁתָּפִין פֶּתַח
chunks.en: A person may not open a door into a shared courtyard
chunks.st: A person may not open an entrance

chunks.en: across from a door, or a window across from a window.
chunks.st: opposite another entrance or a window opposite another window toward a courtyard belonging to partners,
chunks.stMore: so as to ensure that the residents will enjoy a measure of privacy.

chunks.en: If it was small,
chunks.st: If there was a small entrance

chunks.en: he may not make it big.
chunks.st: he may not enlarge it.

chunks.en: One, he may not make it two.
chunks.st: If there was one entrance he may not fashion it into two.

chunks.he: אֲבָל פּוֹתֵחַ הוּא לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים פֶּתַח
chunks.en: But he may open a door facing the public street
chunks.st: But one may open an entrance

chunks.en: across from a door, or a window across from a window.
chunks.st: opposite another entrance or a window opposite another window toward the public domain.

chunks.en: If it was small,
chunks.st: Similarly, if there was a small entrance

chunks.en: he may make it big.
chunks.st: he may enlarge it,

chunks.en: One, he may make it two.
chunks.st: and if there was one entrance he may fashion it into two.

summary: A person may not dig holes under a public road, and Rabbi Eliezer allows it if a strong covering is on top. He may not build beams or balconies sticking out over the public road, but if he buys a house that already has them, he may keep them.

chunks.he: אֵין עוֹשִׂין חָלָל תַּחַת רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: We may not make an empty space under a public road,
chunks.st: One may not form an empty space be-neath the public domain

chunks.en: like pits, ditches and caves.
chunks.st: by digging pits, ditches, or caves.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer allows it if it is strong enough
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer deems it permitted
chunks.stMore: for one to do so, provided that he places a covering strong enough that

chunks.en: that a wagon loaded with stones can go over it.
chunks.st: a wagon laden with stones would be able to tread
chunks.stMore: on it without breaking it, therefore ensuring that the empty space will not cause any damage to those in the public domain.

chunks.he: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין זִיזִין וּגְזֻזְטְרָאוֹת לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: We may not put out beams and balconies over a public road.
chunks.st: One may not extend projections or balconies [ugzuztraot] into the public domain.

chunks.en: But if he wants, he moves his wall back
chunks.st: Rather, if he desired to build one he may draw back

chunks.en: into his own land and puts them out.
chunks.st: into his property by moving his wall, and extend
chunks.stMore: the projection to the end of his property line.

chunks.en: If he bought a courtyard that has beams and balconies,
chunks.st: If one purchased a courtyard in which there are projections and balconies extending into the public domain,

chunks.en: it stays the way it is.
chunks.st: this courtyard retains its presumptive status,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the owner has the acquired privilege of their use, and the court does not demand their removal.
